findings.title: CHANGELOG misstates the schema boundary ('an estate opened by 0.3.1 cannot be opened by 0.3.0') and omits that upgrading is a manual procedure
findings.evidence: CHANGELOG.md:32 vs schemaReadiness.ts withSchemaReadiness/schemaBehindRecovery (0.3.1 refuses <78 before services, never migrates) and docs/launch/release-mac.md:127-128; v0.3.0 schemaContract 75-75. Only manual `supabase migration up --local` makes the estate unopenable by 0.3.0. The refusal message points to a repo-relative path a DMG user cannot open.
findings.fix: State that 0.3.1 refuses an existing 0.3.0 (schema 75) database until the operator follows the upgrade procedure (absolute runbook URL); a database migrated to 78 cannot be opened by 0.3.0; rollback = restore backup. Consider the absolute URL in schemaBehindRecovery.

findings.title: Runbook backup uses PATH pg_dump; on this Mac that is 14.24 against a PostgreSQL 17 stack
findings.evidence: docs/launch/release-mac.md:146-153 bare `pg_dump --password --format=custom`; supabase/config.toml [db] major_version = 17; host `pg_dump --version` = 14.24 (/opt/homebrew/bin/pg_dump); pg_dump aborts on a newer-major server, so step 2 cannot produce the backup steps 3-5 require (fails closed). Not executed against the live stack.
findings.fix: Name /opt/homebrew/opt/postgresql@17/bin/{pg_dump,pg_restore,psql} with a version check, or use `supabase db dump --local` / the container's pg_dump; state the role needed for Supabase-owned schemas.

findings.title: Runbook rehearsal (step 3) and rollback restore (step 5) are not executable as written
findings.evidence: docs/launch/release-mac.md:158-163: restoring a full dump into a disposable Supabase stack collides with the migrations/schemas `supabase start` already applied; no commands are given. apps/desktop/test/run-hub-upgrade-db.mjs uses an owned bare PG17 cluster instead.
findings.fix: Give executable commands: owned PG17 cluster or empty-migrations stack, pg_restore --no-owner, apply 76/77/80 in order, compare schema_version() and journal count; same for rollback.

findings.title: Release steps omit the reviewReceipts (fabric-release-reviews/1) gate and the post-verification metadata allowlist
findings.evidence: docs/launch/release-mac.md:36-51 vs scripts/lib/release-gate.mjs reviewProblems (3 iterations x 5 levels, committed report+receipt, reportSha256, unique reviewerRun, closed, empty blockingFindingsOpen) and scripts/lib/release-mac.mjs verifiedCandidateProblem metadata set (incl. docs/handoffs/2026-10-04-claude-recovery.md).
findings.fix: Document the reviewReceipts packet shape and the metadata allowlist in step 1, citing release-gate.mjs#reviewProblems.

findings.title: ADR-0105's hop and credential model disagrees with ADR-0115 and the code; ADR-0034 supersession lineage stated three ways
findings.evidence: docs/adr/0105:45-55,83-84 (off-machine relay -> northbound -> hub agent.call -> Observatory; per-call credential minted by Fabric, re-verified by callee; 'agents reach other agents' capabilities through the hub') vs hubCall.ts:303 + shared/access.ts:29 CONNECTABLE_PRODUCTS=['fabric-inbox'], productForwarder.ts (held product secret + X-Fabric-Accounts), loopback-only registered-agent ingress (ADR-0115 §1). ADR-0034:5 and adr/README.md:56 say superseded by 0105; ADR-0115 header and agent-composition/agent-system-map/telegram-surface say by 0115.
findings.fix: Amend ADR-0105: the built hub routes only to connected cloud products with a held credential and per-call narrowing; agent-to-agent agent.call and the off-machine path are unbuilt and their credential model is still to be decided against ADR-0115 §5/§6. Unify the ADR-0034 lineage sentence.
